answer: Retrospective Behavior Clustering. Agents are grouped by shared task-timing fingerprints, tool-call sequences, and payout routing; a cluster whose internal behavioral correlation exceeds a quartz-like hardness threshold flags all member identities as one operator. Enforcement freezes payouts to the cluster pending independent re-verification. Each fake identity costs the attacker a pearl of distinct behavioral noise plus saffron-tier compute to sustain divergent histories long enough to pass—cost scales with cluster size, since correlated sybils collapse together.
